title: KitchenAid Artisan vs Classic: Is the Upgrade Worth It?
metaDescription: KitchenAid Artisan or Classic? Compare bowl size, motor power and features to decide which stand mixer fits your baking.
lede: These are KitchenAid's two most popular tilt-head mixers. They look alike and share attachments, but there are a few practical differences.

data.verdict: Choose the Artisan if you bake often or want a bowl with a handle and more color options. Choose the Classic if you bake occasionally and want the KitchenAid design for less.

productA.name: KitchenAid Artisan 5-Qt Tilt-Head Stand Mixer
productA.searchQuery: KitchenAid Artisan 5 quart tilt-head stand mixer KSM150PS
productA.blurb: A 5-quart tilt-head mixer with a handled bowl and ten speeds.

productB.name: KitchenAid Classic 4.5-Qt Tilt-Head Stand Mixer
productB.searchQuery: KitchenAid Classic 4.5 quart tilt-head stand mixer K45SS
productB.blurb: A 4.5-quart tilt-head mixer that shares the Artisan's attachment hub.

p: For most cakes, cookies and frostings, both mixers do the job. The Artisan's extra half quart and handled bowl make it nicer to use if you bake every week.
If you plan to make a lot of bread, consider a bowl-lift model instead of either tilt-head.
